newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil CNI says economy not overheating.
newsitem.headline: Brazil CNI says economy not overheating.

text.p: Brazil's National Industry Confederation (CNI) said Monday fears the economy was beginning to overheat were unfounded.
The CNI said the economy expanded a seasonally-adjusted 2.7 percent in the third quarter of 1996.
"The CNI considers unfounded fears of an overheating in the economy," the statement said.

"Gross domestic product growth in the third quarter of 2.7 percent, compared with the same period in 1995, for example, is still a lower rate than the average seen immediately after the launch of the Real (plan of economic stabilization in June 1994)," it added.
Echoing the government, the CNI pinpointed a credit boom as one of the main causes of a consumer-led recovery.
"According to a CNI study, the trend is for demand to be accommodated," it said, adding there was little expectation the strong pace of economic recovery would continue.
"The industrial statistics show that after a real leap in economic activity in July, the process of recovery has been characterized by a relatively moderate pace in the last months," it said.
The CNI, in its November report on the economy, said inflation was expected to drop further in December, ending the year with consumer inflation slightly above 10 percent.
It also said it expected the operational public sector deficit to end 1996 at about 4.0 percent of gross domestic product after Brazil posted a 3.8 percent of GDP deficit up to end-September.
And the CNI put its estimate for the year-end trade deficit at $4.5 billion. -- Michael Christie, Brasilia newsroom 55-61-2230358
